notes.title: Minor Update 4/21
notes.content:
Just a small update today;

Sound Effects:
Fixed Paper Throwing sound effect not being affected by SFX slider in options.

Levels:
Adjusted the car crash in 2-3 to prevent Softlocking the player inside the crashed truck.

notes.title: Minor Update 4/16
notes.content:
Player:
Camera Flash now fires faster.
Added missing "hit" sound effect for the Spreadshot papers.
Slightly decreased range of base Paper

Enemies:
Lowered Big Uncle's health from 3 to 2, Tall Andrew's from 2 to 1 (Pending further change upon feedback; potentially too easy now)
Added more enemies to 2-2
Adjusted Maggies' collision so the player will kill them if they walk/jump on them, though it will still damage the player.
The Tall Andrew driving the Truck at the end of 2-3 now reacts to getting hit after the truck has crashed.

Levels:
Slightly adjusted multiple enemies' and platforms' positions for more fluid attacks and movement on each level.
Landing on the Powerlooms at the end of 2-2 would take a full life instead of just a heart on lower difficulties; this has been fixed.
Fixed the collision on the scaffolding hanging from the ceiling in 2-3 so the player will not pass through it.

Tutorial:
Relocated and reworded the Jump/Dash tip in the Tutorial.
Added tip for Climbing Ladders and Ducking in the Tutorial.
Fixed Tutorial's Secret Photo not firing correctly when discovered.

Menu Navigation:
Prevented the Selection indicator from appearing too soon on the Continue? Menu

notes.title: Minor Update 4/14
notes.content:
Player Attacks:
-Unlocked Newsie's rate of fire for the base newspaper attack.
-Ink Jars now fire faster to ensure they fire in the direction you're facing when you fire them.

Enemies:
-Lowered Big Nephew and Tandy's Hit Points from 2 to 1.
-Adjusted multiple enemy collisions to prevent completely overlapping one another.

Levels:
-Prevented potential softlocking at the end of 2-1; The concrete tube will now blink momentarily before respawning at its start point after it has completed its roll so you don't have to sacrifice a life or heart to force it to respawn.

Menu Navigation:
-Fixed highlighting selected option on Main, Stage Select, and Difficulty Select Menus (Can no longer highlight one option with the mouse and another with the controller/keyboard)
-Added a "Front Page" indicator to the Stage Select Menu to help track "BREAKING NEWS" unlock progress.

notes.title: Free Demo Now Available
notes.content:
[h3]Welcome to the first look at [i]Page Turner[/i]![/h3]
[i]Page Turner[/i] is my love letter to the classic side-scrolling arcade platformers I grew up with. I’ve always adored this genre, and I wanted to create a game that captures the magic that made me fall in love with it in the first place—from the challenging, fast-paced action of Konami titles like [i]Sunset Riders[/i] and [i]Contra[/i], to the expressive, detailed animations of the [i]Metal Slug[/i] series.

Today’s games offer so much: procedurally generated levels, skill trees, branching narratives, deep upgrade systems, crafting menus—the medium has grown far beyond what I imagined as a kid. And while all of that is amazing... sometimes, I just want to go right and shoot bad guys.

Every level in [i]Page Turner[/i] is handcrafted—from the animations and pixel art to every single piece of set dressing in the environment.

And all you have to do is go right and shoot bad guys.

The game is still in development, and this demo includes three completed stages as both a sneak peek at what’s to come and an opportunity for you, the player, to help shape the final experience. Your thoughts, feedback, and impressions mean the world to me—please consider leaving a review or reaching out to PoppKeys Games. I read every message personally and take your input seriously.

I can’t wait to hear what you think of the game so far—and to see how it evolves over the next year of development.

Thank you so much for playing. I hope you enjoy Level Two of [i]Page Turner[/i].
– Hayden Popp
 Developer, PoppKeys Games
